title: WTT Champions Montpellier draw: Lebrun brothers, Sun Yingsha and Moregard learn openers
standfirst: Félix Lebrun plays Denmark's Anders Lind on Tuesday evening, Sun Yingsha's return starts against Camille Lutz, and Wen Ruibo and Liang Jingkun meet in an all-Chinese first round.
author: michael
body: The draw for WTT Champions Montpellier, made on Sunday, gives the home crowd an eventful start. Félix Lebrun, the world No. 2 and 2024 champion, opens against Denmark's Anders Lind at 18:30 local time on Tuesday, according to the French federation. His brother Alexis, ranked eighth, plays Germany's Patrick Franziska on Wednesday evening.

Three more French men face seeded opponents. Thibault Poret meets defending champion Truls Moregard of Sweden on Tuesday, Flavien Coton plays Korea's Jang Woojin and Simon Gauzy takes on Japan's Tomokazu Harimoto, who won the Asian title in Tashkent on Sunday.
Sora Matsushima, the world No. 1 and top seed, starts against Germany's Dang Qiu. Hugo Calderano, seeded sixth, faces Japan's Hiroto Shinozuka, Rallys reported.

With Wang Chuqin out injured, China's men are spread across the draw. Sohu reported that Wen Ruibo and Liang Jingkun were drawn together in the first round, while Lin Shidong meets Korea's Lim Jonghoon and Xiang Peng plays Dmitrij Ovtcharov. Chinese outlets have given conflicting accounts of who filled the place left by Wang.

In the women's event, top seed Wang Manyu opens against Egypt's Hana Goda. Sun Yingsha, back after injury, plays France's Camille Lutz in Tuesday's midday session. Miwa Harimoto, who has won the last three Champions events, meets Brazil's Bruna Takahashi as she chases a fourth in a row, according to Rallys.

Chen Yi, the new Asian champion, plays Chinese Taipei's Peng Yu-han, and last year's finalist Sabine Winter faces France's Jia Nan Yuan. Prithika Pavade, the leading French woman, meets Japan's Hitomi Sato, the eighth seed.
The event is singles only and runs until Sunday's finals at the Sud de France Arena.
